question: Which reproductive cancer is the most common among women in Nigeria?
explanation: Cervical cancer is the leading gynaecological malignancy in Nigeria, largely due to gaps in screening and HPV prevention. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why do women in low-resource settings often have lower survival rates from reproductive cancers?

options.A: Treatment options are completely unavailable worldwide
options.B: The cancers grow much faster in tropical climates
options.C: Genetic factors make the tumours resistant to all drugs
options.D: They usually present to the hospital with advanced stages

explanation: Late presentation means cancers are often diagnosed only after they have spread, making successful treatment much harder. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which specific high-risk HPV types are most commonly linked to cervical cancer?
explanation: High-risk strains 16 and 18 cause the majority of cervical cancer cases globally. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h2)

question: A client asks why having multiple sexual partners raises her risk of cervical cancer. What is the best explanation?

options.A: It raises her chance of acquiring high-risk human papillomavirus
options.B: It causes chronic physical damage to the internal pelvic organs
options.C: It directly alters her genetic code within the uterine lining
options.D: It permanently stops her ovaries from producing protective hormones

explanation: More partners increase exposure to sexually transmitted infections, particularly high-risk strains of human papillomavirus. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary reason obesity increases the risk of endometrial cancer?

options.A: Excess weight stops the pituitary gland from working
options.B: Obesity causes permanent scarring of the fallopian tubes
options.C: Adipose tissue converts androgens into oestrogen
options.D: Fat cells release toxins that destroy uterine tissue

explanation: Fat tissue produces oestrogen, leading to an imbalance and excessive growth of the uterine lining when not opposed by progesterone. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following inherited gene mutations significantly increases a woman's risk for ovarian cancer?
explanation: Mutations in BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes are well-known hereditary risk factors for breast and ovarian malignancies. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h3)

question: At what stage of life is the HPV vaccine most effective when given to girls?

options.A: After they have been diagnosed with cancer
options.C: During their third trimester of pregnancy

explanation: The vaccine works best when given before any exposure to the human papillomavirus through sexual activity. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention in the context of reproductive cancers?

options.B: Providing surgery after a tumour is found
options.C: Catching early cellular changes with a pap smear
options.D: Stopping the disease from ever developing

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on stopping risk factors and causes so the disease never starts in the body. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h4)

question: What solution is applied to the cervix during a Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) screening?
explanation: Acetic acid is essentially diluted vinegar, which causes abnormal precancerous cells on the cervix to turn white for easy spotting. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h5)

question: A rural health clinic lacks a laboratory to process Pap smears. Which screening method is most appropriate for this setting?
explanation: Visual inspection requires minimal equipment and gives immediate results, making it ideal for low-resource clinics without laboratories. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is opportunistic screening during routine clinic visits effective?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for laboratory testing
options.B: It stops patients from ever developing fibroids
options.C: It ensures that vaccines can be given to elderly women
options.D: It reaches women who might not visit the hospital solely for cancer checks

explanation: Many women only come for pregnancy or family planning, giving midwives a valuable window to offer screening tests. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard responsibility of the midwife in reproductive cancer care?

options.A: Referring clients with suspicious lesions to specialists
options.B: Performing major surgical removal of ovarian tumours

explanation: Major surgeries like tumour removals are performed by gynaecological surgeons, not midwives. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T1#BMP320_U2_T1_h6)
